_note: What .github/workflows/refresh-packs.yml rebuilds after each transfer window, and what a local run does
with no arguments. One entry per generated pack.
search     the query tools/refresh.js gives Wikipedia's list=search; the resolver prints what it picked,
because season-article titles move and get renamed.
out        the pack file to write. Everything here is a snapshot of an article on the run date;
the pack's own note carries the article title, the CC BY-SA licence and the history link.
minClubs   a floor on how many clubs the parse found. A top flight is 16-20 clubs; if the parse
returns fewer, Wikipedia changed its table shape and the pack is wrong, not small.
The job fails instead of committing a truncated league. Set 0 for a deliberately tiny one.
Why only Wikipedia here: a pack built by CI is committed to a public repo, which is redistribution, and
the football APIs with a free tier (football-data.org, API-Football) license their data for *your* app,
not for republishing their database. Facts are not copyrightable, but the EU sui generis database right
covers the investment in the collection regardless — so a licensed provider's whole squad list committed
to a public repo is exactly the thing its terms forbid. Wikipedia (CC BY-SA, attribute it) and
openfootball (public domain) may be redistributed. Keys belong in the player's own localStorage, and a
keyed provider should feed an overlay on their device, never this file.
